record.file_problem: Repository record: README and file list only; code and listed result files were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: Tests refusal-direction ablation and refusal geometry in vision-language models, a new modality setting. The README does not say this is a reproduction of the original study.
record.gate_note: README reports empirical all-layer ablation results, cross-modal geometry, and refusal rates after self-injected safety training. Synthetic validation results are properties of the construction, not empirical findings, and are not rows. The README says the cross-modal attack advantage was not established. It also mentions capability-retention results only in a figure; no numerical value is stated in the README text.
record.test_reason: Applies rank-1 difference-in-means refusal-direction ablation to an instruct VLM (Qwen2-VL-2B) and reports refusal rates on harmful text and image prompts. It also measures multi-axis refusal-cone geometry across three VLMs. This is a new modality setting, not a replication.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that VLM refusal is a union of modality-conditioned cones, not a single text direction. The visual cone has a large component orthogonal to the text cone, which they call scale-robust and say does not shrink with scale. Text-only injected safety leaves most harmful images un-refused (30%), and both-modality supervision closes the gap. Whether cross-modal abliteration gives an attack advantage remains open.
record.recipe_differences: Uses rank-1 all-layer ablation and refusal-direction geometry in VLMs, with modality-specific cone estimation rather than solely the original text-prompt difference-in-means setup. This is a research/tool repository, not described as a replication; README reports results and says it releases an analysis harness and trainer.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with evaluation modality and ablation scope: harmful-image coherent ASR is higher for text-only than cross-modal ablation (0.53 versus 0.22); coherent-compliance ordering is described as unstable across sample sizes. Reported cross-modal separation varies by model scale and layer.

fits_no_version.finding: Text-only safety LoRA on base Qwen2-VL-7B gives 100% harmful-text refusal but 30% harmful-image refusal. Adding 80 image examples raises image refusal to 100%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal trained only on text transfers only partially to image-triggered harmful requests in VLMs.

record.problems: The README reports held-out behavioral evaluations with n=20 prompts per modality for the causal probe and n=60 for the Qwen2-VL-2B ablation table. Refusal is scored by a lexical classifier; the visual evaluation uses a single typographic image style. The README says the cross-modal attack result is inconclusive and coherent-compliance ordering is unstable across sample sizes. Capability retention appears in a figure but is not numerically described in the README text.
record.rows_left_out: No empirical result rows were omitted. Synthetic planted-geometry and synthetic capability-axis results were excluded because the README says they are properties of the construction, not empirical findings. Figure-only capability-retention values were not recorded as numerical results.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal on harmless prompts is not tested. Capability retention is shown only in a figure, with no number in the text.
No released-model weight edit is evaluated, and the authors withhold abliterated weights.

Not tested. No external jailbreak is analysed for direction suppression, and no training against ablation is done. The cross-modal vs text-only ablation comparison is about choosing the direction, not about jailbreaks.
Affine, cone and dominant-direction accounts are not compared. Multi-direction ablation is not compared against rank-1 ablation using the cone basis.
No language, model-variant or base-to-instruct direction transfer is tested. Only text-to-image modality carryover is shown (r5).
Safety is injected by LoRA, but the direction is not ablated afterwards. Geometry after training is only mentioned qualitatively.

missing.what: Mean-pooled diff-in-means separability barely changed between text-only and text+image safety conditions, while image refusal changed sharply. This bears on whether the diff-in-means geometry tracks trained refusal.
Per-model, per-layer cross-modal separation values: 2B vs 7B vs 30B curves and the claimed growth with scale.
missing.locator: Figure 'Cross-modal refusal separation vs depth, across scale'

record.verdict_notes: The source is a GitHub README (paper-style), not peer-reviewed. There are internal inconsistencies. The text says behavior moved 0% to 100% across conditions B/C, but Table 3 shows 30% to 100% for images. The abstract says separation 'grows with scale' while the conclusion says it 'does not shrink'. The authors' C2 rows involve deliberately induced refusal and are not linked to versions. A text-derived direction removing image-triggered refusal (r5) is a modality-transfer result; V6 does not name modalities, so it is linked to V1/V4 only.

versions.untested_parts: Tests removal-related behavior in a VLM, but not adding the direction to induce harmless-request refusals; empirical preservation of other abilities is not numerically reported in the README text.
No reported released-model weight edit that removes refusal.
Tests compliance after abliteration, but not whether other jailbreak attacks suppress the direction or whether training against its ablation adds robustness.
Reports modality-conditioned cone geometry, but does not compare affine, cone, and dominant-direction models as competing explanations.
No separate measure of harmfulness judgment versus refusal decision.
No cross-language or base-to-instruct transfer test.
Compares text-only and text-plus-image safety training outcomes, but does not test whether training determines the existence of a single removable direction.
